title: How do I Spend my Day?

learn.hook: Things in a day happen in order. What comes first?
points: First we wake up. Next we brush. Then we eat breakfast.
We use words like first, next, then and last.
Before means earlier. After means later.
Some things must happen before others.

example.q: Put in order: eat breakfast, wake up, go to school.
example.answer: Wake up, eat breakfast, go to school

learn.reallife: Making chai has an order: boil water, add tea leaves, add milk, then pour.

games.title: True or false?
items: We wear shoes before we wear socks.
Socks go on first, then shoes.
We wash hands before we eat.
We dry ourselves after a bath.
First the bath, then we dry off.
We brush our teeth after we wake up.
First we wake up, then we brush.
We eat a mango before we peel it.
We peel or cut it first, then eat.

quiz.q: What do we do first?
quiz.explain: Socks go on first. Then shoes. Then we run!

quiz.q: Kabir plants a seed. What happens next?
quiz.explain: After planting, we water the seed. The tree grows much later.

quiz.q: Meena eats dinner, then brushes her teeth, then sleeps. What does she do last?
quiz.explain: Sleeping is the last thing in her list.

quiz.q: Which happens before lunch?
quiz.explain: Breakfast is in the morning. Lunch comes after it.

quiz.q: Aisha makes a sandwich. What does she do first?
quiz.explain: She needs bread first. She eats later.

quiz.q: Joseph comes home from school. What does he do after that?
quiz.explain: After coming home, he washes up. The others happen in the morning.

teach.ask: Gappu: I wore my shoes and then tried to put on socks. What went wrong?
teach.praise: Socks first, then shoes! Order matters. Thank you!
teach.nudge: What should come first? What comes after?

learn.hook: Pihu has a busy day! Let us follow her from morning to night.
points: Morning: Pihu wakes up, exercises, brushes her teeth, takes a bath and eats breakfast.
Day: she goes to school, eats lunch with friends and rests.
Evening: she plays and does her homework.
Night: she eats dinner, reads a story and sleeps.

example.q: Pihu brushes her teeth and eats breakfast. Which does she do first?
steps: We brush our teeth soon after waking up.
Breakfast comes after brushing and bath.

learn.reallife: Your day has a morning, a school time, an evening and a night too!

quiz.q: Which does Pihu do in the morning?
quiz.explain: Pihu exercises after waking up in the morning.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up morning and night jobs

quiz.q: When does Pihu eat lunch with her friends?
quiz.explain: Lunch is in the middle of the day, at school.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the parts of the day

quiz.q: What does Pihu do last at night?
quiz.explain: She sleeps after dinner and a story.

quiz.q: Which comes first in the morning?
quiz.explain: We must wake up before doing anything else.

quiz.q: Pihu plays in the park. The sun is going down. When is it?
quiz.explain: The sun goes down in the evening.

quiz.q: Pihu has 3 morning jobs left: bath, breakfast and combing hair. She finishes 1. How many are left?
quiz.explain: 3 take away 1 is 2.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to take away the finished job

teach.ask: Gappu: What does Pihu do in the morning, and what does she do at night?
teach.praise: Wake up and breakfast in the morning, dinner and sleep at night. Great!
teach.nudge: What is the first thing Pihu does? What is the last?

learn.hook: What do you do every single day? That is your routine!
points: A routine is what we do every day, in the same order.
We brush our teeth in the morning and again at night before bed.
Many of us bathe in the morning.
Tell your routine with words like first, then, after that and at night.

example.q: Put Riya's morning in order: bath, wake up, breakfast, brush teeth.
example.answer: Wake up, brush teeth, bath, breakfast

learn.reallife: A good routine keeps us healthy and on time for school.

games.title: True or false?
items: We should brush our teeth twice a day.
In the morning and at night.
A routine is done in a new order every day.
A routine is done the same way each day.
We eat dinner before we wake up.
Dinner is at night, long after waking up.
Many of us take a bath in the morning.
A morning bath gets us fresh for school.

items.text: We brush our teeth in the morning and at ___.
I eat ___ before going to school.

quiz.q: When should we brush our teeth?
quiz.explain: Brushing twice, morning and night, keeps teeth healthy.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the healthy habit

quiz.q: What is a routine?
options: Things we do every day in the same order
quiz.explain: A routine repeats every day.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a routine with a special event

quiz.q: Kabir's morning: wake up, brush, bath, ___, school. What is missing?
quiz.explain: We eat breakfast before school.
quiz.mistake: Puts a night job in the morning

quiz.q: Aisha brushes her teeth 2 times a day. How many times in 2 days?
quiz.explain: 2 times on day 1 and 2 times on day 2: 2 + 2 = 4.

quiz.q: Which is part of a night routine?
quiz.explain: We change into night clothes before bed.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up day and night jobs

quiz.q: Joseph does homework at 5 o'clock and plays at 6 o'clock. Which comes first?
quiz.explain: 5 o'clock comes before 6 o'clock.

teach.ask: Gappu: Tell me your routine! When do you brush your teeth?
teach.praise: Brush in the morning and at night! What a healthy routine!
teach.nudge: Do you brush only once? When else?

learn.hook: The sun rises, the sun sets. Our day has parts!
points: Morning: the sun comes up. We wake up and go to school.
Afternoon: the sun is high. We eat lunch.
Evening: the sun goes down. We play outside.
Night: it is dark. We see the moon and sleep.

example.q: Riya sees the moon and stars. She goes to bed. What part of the day is it?
steps: Moon and stars come out when it is dark.
We sleep when it is dark.

learn.reallife: We say 'Good morning' when we wake up and 'Good night' before sleeping.

games.title: Match the time of day
pairs: Sun sets, play in the park

quiz.q: When do we usually wake up?
quiz.explain: The sun rises in the morning. We wake up then.

quiz.q: When can we see the moon and stars?
quiz.explain: The sky is dark at night. Then we see stars.
quiz.mistake: Thinks stars shine in the day sky

quiz.q: Arjun eats lunch when the sun is high up. What part of the day is it?
quiz.explain: Lunch time, with the sun high, is the afternoon.

quiz.q: The sun is going down. Birds fly home. When is it?
quiz.explain: The sun sets in the evening.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the sun sets in the morning

quiz.q: Which comes just after morning?
quiz.explain: Morning, then afternoon, then evening, then night.

quiz.q: What do we say before going to sleep?
quiz.explain: We sleep at night, so we say good night.
quiz.mistake: Picks the wrong greeting for the time

teach.ask: Gappu: Why do you say 'Good morning' and 'Good night'?
teach.praise: Morning is when the sun rises. Night is dark, time to sleep!
teach.nudge: When does the sun come up? When is it dark?

learn.hook: Some jobs are quick. Some take a long time!
points: Blinking takes a very short time.
Brushing teeth takes a few minutes.
A school day takes many hours.
Growing a mango tree takes years!

example.q: Which takes longer: drinking a glass of water or watching a cricket match?
steps: Drinking water takes a few seconds.
A cricket match takes many hours.

learn.reallife: A train trip to Nani's house takes longer than a walk to the shop.

quiz.q: Which takes less time?
quiz.explain: A sneeze is over in a second. We sleep for many hours.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up less and more time

quiz.q: Which takes the longest?
quiz.explain: A mango tree takes years to grow.

quiz.q: Which takes more time?
quiz.explain: A cricket match lasts many hours. Washing hands is quick.

quiz.q: Riya walks to the park gate. Harpreet walks all around the big park. They walk at the same speed. Who takes longer?
quiz.explain: Harpreet walks much farther. A longer walk takes more time.

quiz.q: Which can you do in one clap's time?
quiz.explain: A blink is as quick as a clap.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which jobs are quick

quiz.q: Which takes longer?
quiz.explain: Making rangoli takes a long time. Opening a door is quick.

teach.ask: Gappu: Does eating a laddoo take longer than growing a tree?
teach.praise: Ha! Eating is quick. Growing a tree takes years!
teach.nudge: Which one is quick? Which one takes a long time?

learn.hook: Hot sun, heavy rain, cold mornings! Why does the weather change?
points: India has seasons: summer, monsoon (rainy), winter and spring.
Summer is hot. We wear cotton clothes and use fans.
In the monsoon it rains a lot. We need umbrellas and raincoats.
Winter is cold. We wear sweaters. Spring brings new leaves and flowers.

example.q: Riya takes her umbrella and raincoat to school. Which season is it?
steps: Umbrellas and raincoats keep us dry.
We need them when it rains a lot.

learn.reallife: In summer we drink cold lassi. In winter we eat hot gajar halwa.

games.title: Summer or winter?
items: Sitting in the sun to keep warm

quiz.q: Which season is very hot?
quiz.explain: Summer is the hottest season.

quiz.q: Which do you need in the monsoon?
quiz.explain: It rains a lot, so we need an umbrella.
quiz.mistake: Picks winter clothes for the rainy season

quiz.q: Kabir wears a sweater and a woollen cap. Which season is it?
quiz.explain: Sweaters keep us warm when it is cold.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up hot and cold seasons

quiz.q: In which season do many trees get new leaves and flowers?
quiz.explain: After winter, spring brings fresh leaves and flowers.

quiz.q: Which is a summer treat?
quiz.explain: Mangoes ripen in summer and cold lassi cools us down.

quiz.q: How many seasons did we learn: summer, monsoon, winter and spring?
quiz.explain: Count them: 1, 2, 3, 4.

teach.ask: Gappu: It is raining and raining! Which season is it, and what should I carry?
teach.nudge: What do we carry when it rains a lot?

learn.hook: Every season has its own food, clothes and festivals!
points: Write the season names: summer, monsoon, winter, spring.
Match a picture to its season: dark rain clouds go with the monsoon.
Foods we enjoy: mangoes and lassi in summer, hot soup and peanuts in winter.
Festivals come in seasons too: Holi in spring, Lohri and Pongal in winter.
Draw or paste your favourite season food and festival.

example.q: People fly kites on Makar Sankranti in cold January. Which season is it?

learn.reallife: Make a chart with four boxes, one for each season, and paste a food and a festival in each.

items.text: Rain, rain, rain! It is the ___ season.
Sweaters and shawls come out in ___.
Flowers bloom after winter. It is ___.

quiz.q: Which picture goes with the monsoon?
options: A dry field under a hot sun
quiz.explain: The monsoon brings dark clouds and rain.

quiz.q: Which is a good food for a cold winter day?
quiz.explain: Warm food keeps us warm in winter.

quiz.q: Holi comes in which season?
quiz.explain: Holi is the spring festival of colours.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the festival with its season

quiz.q: Which festival comes in winter?
quiz.explain: Lohri is in January, in winter.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the festival with its season

quiz.q: Which word is the name of a season?
quiz.explain: Monsoon is a season. Monday is a day. Morning is a time of day.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up seasons, days and times of day

quiz.q: Meena pastes 2 summer foods and 3 winter foods on her chart. How many pictures?
quiz.explain: 2 and 3 make 5.

teach.ask: Gappu: What do you like to eat in summer, and what do you wear in winter?
teach.praise: Mangoes in summer, sweaters in winter. Yum and cosy!
teach.nudge: What is the weather like in summer? And in winter?
